items.text: The song ends. Nobody speaks for a while.
The child promises to teach the song to other children.
The parent thanks the elder, then carries the baby home.
The elder laughs and says the ancestors would be horrified by the new crab verse. The child looks immensely proud.
The elder hums one last line, quietly enough that only the nearest listeners hear it.

intro.name: The old melody
intro.text:
As the sun begins to set, an elderly villager, (Elder), sits near the village's gathering place, humming an old melody.
A child, (Child), asks where the song came from.
(Elder) says that (elder.he/she) learned it from {a parent|a childhood friend|a teacher|someone who is no longer alive}. The song was once sung {during storms|at weddings|to soothe frightened children|while waiting for boats to return}.
A nearby parent, (Parent), pauses with a sleeping baby in (parent.his/her) arms. (parent.He/She) recognizes {one line|the rhythm|the melody|none of it, but listens anyway}.

text_only.reason: rule 8: VV1 has no Devotion skill; the source allows 'narrative-only'

dev1.text: The elder forgets a verse. The parent remembers it, and they finish the song together.

dev2.text: The child invents an absurd extra verse about a dancing crab. The elder is scandalized for precisely three seconds.

dev3.text: The elder explains that the song used to be sung by someone (elder.he/she) misses. The child listens without interrupting.

dev4.text: The baby wakes and begins crying. The parent hums the melody, and the baby gradually settles.

dev5.text: The elder sings terribly off-key. The child joins in, somehow making the song even worse. Nobody asks them to stop.

dev6.text: The child asks whether the elder will always remember the song. The elder says, "I hope so. But perhaps you can remember it too."
